title: Wave-Particle Duality in Quantum Mechanics
text:
The concept of wave-particle duality posits that all quantum entities exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties. For instance, electrons display interference patterns characteristic of waves when measured over an extended area, yet their interactions often manifest as discrete packets of energy (quanta) typical of particles.

This inherent duality challenges classical understanding, suggesting that matter is not strictly one or the other, but rather exists in a superposition of states. The act of observation itself is critical, causing the superposition to collapse into a definable state, a phenomenon known as wave function collapse.

Understanding this principle requires accepting that reality at the quantum level is fundamentally probabilistic rather than deterministic.
